sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 26.0% a year from $4,319 million in FY2016 to $34,639 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F231].
The path was not smooth: revenue rose 68.3% in FY2021 and 43.6% in FY2022, then fell 3.9% in FY2023 before recovering 13.7% and 34.3% [D258][D314][D370][D426][D483].
The FY2022 step change came largely from the Xilinx acquisition, which added Embedded revenue and lifted total assets 444.2% [D322][P41].
FY2023's decline reflected a 25% drop in Client revenue on weak PC demand and inventory correction, partly offset by Embedded [P35].
FY2025's 34.3% growth was driven by Data Center and Client and Gaming, partly offset by a 3% decline in Embedded [D483][P15].
Data Center reached 48.0% of revenue in FY2025 and contributed 15.7pp of the 34.3% growth [D692][D694][D483].
Data Center revenue rose 32% to $16.6 billion on strong demand for EPYC processors and Instinct GPU accelerators [P13].
Client and Gaming contributed 19.0pp in FY2025, with Client at 30.7% of revenue and Gaming at 11.3% [D701][D754][D761].
Client revenue rose 51% on a 31% increase in processor unit shipments and a 15% rise in average selling price [P10].
Operating income grew 94.4% against 34.3% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 20.3% [D484][D483][D511].
Gross margin of 49.5% is the window high against a 44.7% median, while operating margin of 10.7% sits above its 7.2% median but far below the 22.2% FY2021 peak [F40][D800][D801][F60][D795][D794].
FY2025 gross margin rose only 0.2pp as product mix gains were offset by about $440 million of MI308 inventory and export-control charges [D498][P14].
The FY2025 operating margin gain of 3.3pp came from cost of revenue (+0.2pp), R&D (+1.7pp) and other lines (+2.6pp), partly offset by SG&A (-1.2pp) [D499][D513][D514][D516][D515].
SG&A rose 48.9% and R&D rose 25.3% in FY2025 [D503][D502].
Net margin of 12.5% exceeded operating margin because a $103 million tax benefit and $577 million of other income lifted net income [F80][F60][P4][P5].
Operating cash flow of $7,709 million and free cash flow of $6,735 million were 1.78x and 1.55x net income, against a 1.17x free-cash-flow median [F110][F130][D470][D471][D810].
Free cash flow margin of 19.4% matches the FY2021 high of 19.6% and far exceeds the 6.5% median [D467][D803][D804].
Operating cash flow was reduced by a $2.2 billion inventory build to support Data Center product ramps [P3].
Capex of $974 million was 2.8% of revenue and 1.87x D&A, the highest ratio in the window [F120][D466][D472].
Net cash reached $6,456 million, or 18.6% of revenue, the 100th percentile against six semis peers whose median is -13.9% [D476][D477][D826][D827].
Total debt rose 138.0% to $4,096 million after $1.5 billion of notes were issued in March 2025 [D475][D508][P6].
Buybacks of $1,316 million were 19.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count was flat at -0.1% [D478][D479][D506].
The current ratio of 2.85x is the window high against a 2.19x median [F210][D812][D813].
Revenue fell 3.9% in FY2023, the only decline in the window, on weak PC demand and inventory correction [R1][D370][P35].
Total debt rose 138.0% in FY2025 to $4,096 million, though net cash still rose to $6,456 million [R2][D475][D508][D476].
The effective tax rate swung to -2.5% from 18.8% on an $853 million uncertain-tax-position release, flattering net income [R4][D469][D412][P4].
Three lines were later recast: FY2024 SG&A, FY2023 receivables and FY2017 R&D; the pack uses first-reported values [R5][R6][R7].
Watch operating margin against the 10.7% FY2025 level and the 22.2% FY2021 high; a move back above 22.2% would confirm the margin recovery [F60][D794].
Watch Data Center growth against the 32.2% FY2025 rate; a fall below it would reverse the driver of the latest year [D693].
Watch days inventory outstanding, at 165 days versus the 93-day FY2019 level; a further rise would signal demand outrunning sell-through [D481][D145].
